metadata.description: Ground-truth fault scenarios for Online Boutique v0.10.5. Used by eval/benchmark.py to score zero_shot / vector_rag / agentic_graphrag on RQ1 (root-cause accuracy + MTTR) and RQ2 (blast-radius F1). Each scenario was verified end-to-end against the live agent in Phase 5.
metadata.stack: Online Boutique v0.10.5 (Docker Compose, boutique-sim network)
metadata.blast_radius_definition: All services that transitively DEPENDS_ON the root cause (includes loadgenerator, the synthetic traffic driver).
metadata.last_updated: 2026-06-23 (S-04 added: multi-hop variant for RQ1 root-cause accuracy stress test)

alert.message: cartservice reporting cache errors — redis-cart evicting keys under memory pressure
gRPC connection refused to productcatalogservice — container unreachable
Network partition — paymentservice unreachable from checkoutservice

ground_truth.remediation_note: container/restart.sh reattaches the target to boutique-sim before restart; a plain restart does NOT reverse docker network disconnect.

scenarios.name: Redis OOM — Multi-Hop (ambiguous frontend alert, root at depth 3)

alert.message: frontend health check degraded — /cart and /checkout returning 5xx, elevated latency on multiple cart-related requests

ground_truth.multi_hop_note: Root cause is 3 DEPENDS_ON hops from the alerting service. Alert message describes only observable frontend symptoms — it does not name redis-cart, cartservice, or any intermediate service. A system without graph topology must identify the root cause from symptom description alone.

verified.note: Expected via Q1 graph traversal: same 3-hop DEPENDS_ON path as S-01 (frontend→checkoutservice→cartservice→redis-cart). Q1 deterministically returns redis-cart when redis-cart is unhealthy in Neo4j. No live Phase 5 run recorded for this specific alert message variant; MTTR estimated from S-01 (6.3s). The distinguishing feature of this scenario vs S-01 is the alert message — S-04 tests whether baselines can identify a depth-3 root cause from frontend-only symptom description.

closed_loop_scenarios.description: Phase 9 closed-loop scenarios — detection by the telemetry collector (not the injector), real post-execution verification, and NEXT_IF_FAIL fallback. These are NOT part of the RQ1/RQ2 baseline benchmark above (baselines have no detection/execution layer); they validate the autonomous remediation loop end-to-end. The injector only breaks things; simulation/telemetry_collector.py detects and raises the alert.

scenarios.name: Persistent Redis OOM — NEXT_IF_FAIL fallback chain
scenarios.detection: telemetry collector: redis maxmemory capped at 1mb (survives docker restart)

verified.note: First time NEXT_IF_FAIL (Q3) executed; both SOPs gated by real verification.

scenarios.name: Stale Data — activates Redis_Flush_SOP via its real trigger
scenarios.detection: telemetry collector: anomalously large volatile keyspace (expires >= 200)

scenarios.name: High CPU — non-restart remediation (cgroup throttle)
scenarios.detection: telemetry collector: docker stats CPU% >= 80 on adservice
expected_chain: AdService_CPU_Throttle_SOP (docker update --cpus=0.1; real-verify confirms NanoCpus cap)

scenarios.name: External pause — dashboard reflects real health, agent auto-resolves
scenarios.detection: telemetry collector: container status != running -> CRASH_LOOPING

verified.note: Proves the dashboard reflects REAL container health, not faked graph state.

deep_cascade_scenarios.description: Section 2 — deep-cascade root-cause scenarios. Each fires an alert from the FAR end of a dependency chain with a SURFACE symptom that names neither the root nor any intermediate-cause service (verified by an automated leak audit). They stress root-cause LOCALISATION: zero-shot (B1) and vector-RAG (B2) baselines each predict a shallow/named service and fail; only the graph's Q1 multi-hop traversal reaches the true deep root. Online Boutique's topology genuinely tops out at depth 3-4 (shortest path to redis-cart from loadgenerator is 3; Q1 traces the longer 4-hop chain), so depth is reported honestly as 3-4. The agent resolves each end-to-end via 'symptom localises, root's real condition remediates': Q1 finds the root, Q2 falls back from the surface error_type to the root's telemetry-synced condition to select the SOP. error_type=DEGRADED is a generic, no-hint, valid status used so the same alert drives both the baseline comparison and live POST /alert resolution.

scenarios.name: Deep cascade — generic storefront failure (root 3-4 hops at redis-cart)

alert.message: Load test alert: synthetic traffic against the web storefront is returning a sharply elevated HTTP 5xx error rate and high p99 latency; request success rate fell from ~99% to ~62% over 5 minutes.

verified.note: POST /alert -> Q1 redis-cart depth 4 -> Q2 matched_on=OOM_KILLED via_root_condition=True -> real verify maxmemory=0. Independently confirmed redis recovered.

scenarios.name: Deep cascade — checkout-flow failure (root 3 hops at redis-cart via checkout)

alert.message: Checkout flow degraded — order placement requests are returning HTTP 500 at roughly a 40% rate and purchase completion is failing for a large share of user sessions over the last few minutes.

verified.note: Q1 from frontend -> redis-cart depth 3; same OOM root-condition fallback + Redis_Restart_SOP as DC-01.

scenarios.name: Deep cascade — recommendation-widget failure (root 3 hops at productcatalogservice)

alert.message: Personalized recommendation widgets across the storefront are returning empty results or erroring; the recommendations panel fails to populate on home and detail pages.

verified.note: POST /alert -> Q1 productcatalogservice depth 3 -> Q2 matched_on=CRASH_LOOPING via_root_condition=True -> real verify running+on-network. Independently confirmed exited->running.

deep_cascade_scenarios.summary: 3 distinct cascade shapes, 2 distinct roots (redis-cart, productcatalogservice), 2 alerting services (loadgenerator, frontend), 3 distinct symptoms, and 3 DISTINCT baseline failure predictions (frontend / checkoutservice / recommendationservice). GraphRAG root accuracy 3/3; baseline root accuracy 0/3.

unsupported_faults.reason: Online Boutique v0.10.5 images are distroless and lack tc/iproute2, so `tc qdisc netem delay` cannot be injected. fault_injector.inject_high_latency() detects this and no-ops with a warning. Excluded from the evaluation set; service_crash and network_partition cover the same upstream-dependent alerting path.
